name: High pull and pulls
pattern: Explosive hip and knee extension with a shrug, then the elbows lead the weight up to chest height. No catch.
setup: Clean-width grip (snatch-wide for a snatch-grip pull), arms straight.
Stand tall with the bar at mid-thigh, or start from the floor for a sumo pull.
Shoulders slightly over the bar, back flat, chest up.

steps.text: Hinge so the bar slides to just above your knees, knees steady.
Knees and hips move forward under the bar as the torso rises.
Drive hips, knees and ankles straight and shrug hard.
Elbows lead the bar up close to your body to chest height.
Lower the bar to your thighs, softening the knees.

cues.why: Lower body extension produces the power; jump shrug and high pull both make more power than the hang power clean.

cues.cue: Stay tall: do not dip to reach the bar.
cues.why: Bending the knees again to meet the bar at chest height is the main error in the high pull.

cues.cue: Elbows high and out, no higher than your shoulders.
cues.why: Keeping the bar at chest height avoids pinching the shoulder at the top.
A close bar keeps the pull vertical and efficient.
Protects the lower back as load increases.

breathing: Breathe in and brace before the hinge, out once the bar is back down.

mistakes.name: Dipping under
mistakes.looks: Knees bend again as the bar reaches the chest.
mistakes.fix: Finish tall on your toes; use a lighter load.
mistakes.why: It turns the pull into a sloppy catch and cuts the extension.

mistakes.name: Arms do the work
mistakes.looks: Hips and knees barely move; the bar is rowed up.
mistakes.fix: Drive the floor away and shrug before the arms bend.
mistakes.why: Without the jump it becomes an upright row and loses its power training.

mistakes.name: Elbows too high
mistakes.looks: The bar comes up past the collarbone with elbows above the shoulders.
mistakes.fix: Stop the bar at nipple to chest height.
mistakes.why: Arm raise far above 90° with inward rotation can pinch the shoulder.

safety: Shoulder pain: stop at a jump shrug (no arm pull).
Sumo deadlift high pull from the floor: keep the back flat; it is common in conditioning workouts when tired, so cap reps.

variants.change: No arm pull: jump and shrug, land softly with bent knees. Highest power of the three hang derivatives.
From the floor, finish with extension and shrug only; loads may exceed the clean or snatch max.
Wide stance, narrow grip inside the knees, start from the floor.
One bell held in both hands between wide feet.
Rope from a low pulley; keep the jump small and the pull smooth.
Dumbbells at the thighs, elbows lead up and out.

subtypes.name: Sumo deadlift high pull
subtypes.change: Wide stance with toes out, narrow grip, pull from the floor.

subtypes.name: Jump shrug
subtypes.change: Same hang and extension, leave the floor with a shrug, arms stay straight.

metrics.label: Knee bend when the bar reaches the chest

motion.basis: Technique and the dipping error from suchomel2015; power ranking of hang derivatives from suchomel2014 and suchomel2017a. Joint angles are estimates from coaching descriptions, not measured values.
